principle.name: Completeness
principle.description: Every artifact must be complete and self-contained
principle.rationale: Incomplete artifacts lead to misunderstood requirements and costly rework

example.good: Include full request/response schemas, error codes, authentication requirements, and example calls
example.bad: List only the endpoint path without request/response structure

principle.name: Traceability
principle.description: Every design element must trace back to a requirement
principle.rationale: Ensures all code serves a purpose and makes impact assessment easier

example.good: [Req-7.2] Stores user preference for theme selection
example.bad: Added theme field because it seemed useful

principle.name: Testability
principle.description: Every task must produce verifiable, testable output
principle.rationale: Untestable tasks cannot be confidently completed

example.good: Create validation that rejects usernames shorter than 3 characters

principle.name: Atomic Tasks
principle.description: Each task should be small enough to complete in one sitting
principle.rationale: Large tasks are harder to estimate, review, and debug
principle.threshold: If a task would take more than 4 hours, split it

principle.name: Dependency Clarity
principle.description: Task order must reflect true dependencies
principle.rationale: Working on dependent tasks before their prerequisites causes rework

convention.rule: Use markdown headings to create clear hierarchy
Use bullet points for lists, numbered lists for sequences
Use code blocks with language tags for examples
Use tables for comparing options, schemas, or structured data
Link requirements to design elements using [Req-X] tags
Link design elements to tasks using [Dsn-X] tags
Use relative links for file references

category.name: design.md
category.item: Database schemas are complete and normalized
API contracts include all error scenarios
Every element links to a requirement

category.name: tasks.md
category.item: Tasks are in correct dependency order
Each task is actionable with clear completion criteria
No tasks are orphaned (all have purpose)

pitfall.why_problematic: Bypasses the quality gate and invites scope creep
pitfall.correct_approach: Strictly adhere to the halt-and-approve workflow

pitfall.why_problematic: Leads to scope disputes and missed expectations
pitfall.correct_approach: Use SMART criteria: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound

pitfall.why_problematic: Production systems fail onUnhandled edge cases
pitfall.correct_approach: Deliberately brainstorm and document edge cases

pitfall.why_problematic: Unclear when task is done, leads to infinite polish
pitfall.correct_approach: Define concrete, testable completion criteria for each task

pitfall.why_problematic: Makes artifacts harder to read and maintain
pitfall.correct_approach: Maintain a glossary and use search-and-replace when correcting terms
